title: 100 Emails
comparison: ~20 kg/year if you send 10000 emails
comment: Most of that comes from the data centres storing and routing your messages, not your phone. I assumed it was the phone.

title: 10 Hour Streaming
comparison: Streaming accounts for ~80% of internet traffic
comment: The digital sector produces 4% of global GHG right now, and that's projected to reach 14% by 2040.

title: 1 Banana
comparison: ~20 kg/year eating one every second day
comment: One of the lowest-footprint foods you can buy, bananas travel by ship not plane and need no packaging.

title: 1kg Potatoes
comparison: ~25 kg/year on average per person in Ireland
comment: People in Ireland eat between 85 kg and 96 kg of potatoes a year. I didn't expect the humble spud to add up to that much.

title: 1 Bag of Tayto
comparison: ~6 kg/year if you have one every day
comment: Crisp production takes a lot of energy, and the packaging adds to the footprint too.

title: 1 Pint of Guinness
comparison: ~30 kg/year for a pint a day
comment: Diageo, the company behind Guinness, has committed to net zero operations by 2030. Fair play to them, that's one to watch.

title: 1kg Irish Butter
comparison: ~33 kg/year at typical household use
comment: Irish dairy has one of the lower emissions intensities in Europe, but it's still significant.

title: 1kg Cheddar Cheese
comparison: Cheese requires ~10L of milk per kg
comment: Dairy is Ireland's biggest source of agricultural emissions. I didn't expect cheese to be the bigger story than beef here.

title: 1kg Chicken
comparison: A 150 g chicken breast is about 1.5 kg.
comment: I looked for Irish chicken figures and found none I trust. Much of the feed is imported, so I use the world average.
source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018 (Poultry Meat), full life cycle incl. land use
note: Changed from 6.9 (no documented source) on 27 Sep 2026. No Irish poultry footprint from Teagasc, Bord Bia or EPA; Irish broilers rely on imported soya and grain. OWID 9.87 = LUC 3.51 + farm 0.93 + feed 2.45 + post-farm 1.52 + losses 1.45.

title: 1 Litre Oat Milk
comparison: vs ~1.3 kg for Irish cow's milk
comment: Oat milk uses about 80% less land and 60% less water than dairy milk. Grand alternative if you ask me.

title: 1 Litre Cow's Milk
comparison: About 475 kg a year for a household using a litre a day.
comment: Irish milk is among the lowest-carbon in the world, well under half the global average at the farm gate. All that grass helps.
source: Teagasc National Farm Survey Sustainability Report (about 1 kg CO2e per litre at the farm gate, against a global average of about 2.5), plus processing, packaging and transport
note: Changed from 3.2 (Poore & Nemecek global average) to 1.3 on 27 Sep 2026 at Fabien's request: Irish milk is about 1.2 to 1.4 kg CO2e per litre once processing and distribution are added to the Teagasc farm-gate figure. Only 4% from 1 Sliced Pan (1.25), so the two are never dealt together.
world_source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018 (milk, full life cycle incl. land use) (3.15, rounded)

title: 1 Washing Load
comparison: Most emissions come from the energy to warm up the water
comment: Washing at 30°C instead of 40°C cuts energy use by about 40%, and modern detergents work just as well.

title: 10 Min Shower
comparison: ~760 kg CO₂/year if you shower daily
comment: Cutting a 10 minute shower to 4 minutes roughly halves the footprint, and it saves on hot water bills too.

title: 1 Tumble Dryer Load
comparison: ~280 kg/year if used daily
comment: Air drying clothes saves the full amount. Dryers are among the most energy hungry appliances in the home.

title: 1 Dishwasher Cycle
comparison: Similar footprint to a washing machine load at 40°C
comment: Roughly equivalent to a washing machine load. Newer A-rated models use significantly less energy though.

title: Heating Home 1 Day
comparison: ~4400 kg/year for a typical Irish home
comment: Over half of Irish homes still heat with gas or oil. Heat pumps cut this by 50 to 70%, which is a big jump.

title: LED Bulb vs Halogen
comparison: Switching all bulbs in a home saves ~80 kg/year
comment: LED bulbs use about 80% less energy, and halogen bulbs are now banned for sale in the EU.

title: 1 Pizza
comparison: ~78 kg/year if you eat one every week
comment: The cheese topping accounts for nearly half the pizza's total footprint. I checked twice because that seemed high.

title: 1 Cheeseburger
sub: 100 g Irish beef patty, bun and cheese
comparison: Eaten once a week, about 200 kg a year.
comment: The beef patty is about nine tenths of this burger's footprint. The bun and the cheese barely register.
source: Derived from the 1kg Beef (35) and 1kg Cheddar (9.8) cards and OWID wheat bread (1.57)
note: Changed from 3.2 on 27 Sep 2026. Patty 0.100 x 35 = 3.50; bun 0.080 x 1.57 = 0.13; cheese 0.020 x 9.8 = 0.20; salad, sauce, wrap about 0.10; total 3.93. A 45 g fast-food patty would be about 2.0.

title: 100km by Train
comparison: About 4x less than the same trip by car
comment: Irish Rail has committed to full electrification by 2030, so the footprint will fall further as the grid gets greener.

title: 1kg of Coffee Beans
comparison: ~180 kg/year at 1 kg/month
comment: Coffee production takes a lot of water. I didn't realise my morning coffee had that kind of footprint behind it.
action_title: Switch to a certified sustainable coffee brand
action_desc: Look for Rainforest Alliance or organic certification next time you buy beans or ground coffee.
action_saving: Reduces water use and land pressure per kg of beans

title: 100km by Car
comparison: ~4000 kg/year at 16000 km driven
comment: That excludes manufacturing, and it also causes local air pollution and health impacts.
action_title: Replace one car journey with public transport this week
action_desc: Even one return trip by bus or train instead of car saves roughly 50 kg CO₂ over the year if done weekly.
action_saving: ~50 kg CO₂ saved/year if done weekly

title: 1kg Lamb
comparison: A 150 g portion of lamb is about 6 kg.
comment: I hoped Irish grass would make lamb greener. The Irish figures land close to the world average. Sheep burp a lot of methane.
action_title: Try one lamb-free week this month
action_desc: Lamb has one of the highest footprints of any meat. Swapping it for chicken or legumes makes a real difference.
action_saving: ~40 kg CO₂ saved per kg avoided
source: Full life cycle incl. land use: Teagasc Sheep LCA and NFS Sustainability Report 2024 (farm), Poore & Nemecek 2018 via OWID (land-use change, post-farm, losses)
note: Changed from 28 on 27 Sep 2026 (full LCA, Fabien). Farm about 11 kg CO2e per kg liveweight (Teagasc lowland flock 10.8, only about 4% below the global 11.3), 93% to meat, kill-out 0.46 x yield 0.71, OWID GWP = 36.5; land-use change +0.65; post-farm +2.9; losses x1.174 = 47 (41 on Teagasc GWP). OWID lamb is 39.7. Recommended 40, range 36-47. Irish lamb shows no advantage over the global figure.
world_source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018 (lamb and mutton, full life cycle incl. land use)

title: 1 Pair Leather Shoes
comparison: Same as driving a petrol car about 120 km
comment: The tanning process for leather is highly polluting, and most leather is a by-product of the beef industry.
action_title: Buy your next pair of shoes second-hand or from a sustainable brand
action_desc: Manufacturing one pair of leather shoes produces ~30 kg CO₂. Second-hand or vegan alternatives cut that dramatically.
action_saving: Up to 30 kg CO₂ saved per pair

title: 1 Fast Fashion T-Shirt
comparison: Same as leaving a phone charger plugged in for 6 months
comment: About 96% of cotton is grown with pesticides, and fast fashion creates 92 million tonnes of waste a year.

title: 1 Pair of Jeans
comparison: Same footprint as driving ~130 km in a petrol car
comment: It takes about 7500 litres of water to make one pair, equivalent to about 7 years of drinking water.

title: 1kg Beef
comparison: A 100 g serving is about 3.5 kg, and the kilo is about 60 times the 1kg of lentils card (0.58 kg).
comment: Irish beef comes in below the world average, but it's still one of the heaviest foods I've found. Kilo for kilo, sixty times lentils.
action_desc: Beef is the highest-impact common food. Replacing it with chicken, fish or plant protein just once a week adds up.
action_saving: ~35 kg CO₂ saved per kg avoided
source: Full life cycle incl. land use: Teagasc NFS Sustainability Report 2024 and Bord Bia SBLAS 2023 (farm), Poore & Nemecek 2018 via OWID (land-use change, processing, transport, retail, packaging, losses)
note: Changed from 60 on 27 Sep 2026 (full LCA, Fabien). Farm about 10 kg CO2e per kg liveweight, 93% allocated to meat, kill-out 0.56 x retail yield 0.72, re-weighted to OWID GWP (+15%) = 26.5; land-use change +1.3 (imported feed, OWID proxy); post-farm +2.9; losses x1.17 = about 36 (32 on Teagasc GWP). Range 28-40. OWID beef herd is 99.5; about a third of the gap is land-use change, most is farm and feed efficiency. Soil sequestration not netted. Lowest-in-the-world claims are not supported (JRC data is 2002-04; GLEAM puts Ireland about 5% below the EU).
world_source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018 (beef herd, full life cycle incl. land use)

title: 1 Smartphone
comparison: Same as charging your phone every day for 185 years
comment: About 80% of a phone's lifetime footprint comes from manufacturing, not from using it.
action_title: Keep your current phone for one more year
action_desc: Manufacturing a new smartphone produces ~70 kg CO₂. The best phone for the planet is the one you already own.

title: 1 Bicycle
comparison: Same as a return Dublin–Belfast train journey
comment: Manufacturing is the main footprint, once built a bike produces zero emissions per km.
action_desc: Manufacturing a new bicycle uses ~96 kg CO₂. Second-hand bikes cut that to near zero, and save money too.

title: Dublin–Holyhead Ferry
comparison: A return flight Dublin–Manchester emits ~3x more CO₂
comment: Ferry and train to the UK is often just as quick once you factor in airport check-in, and it's far lower carbon.

title: 1 Rasher of Bacon
comparison: One a day for a year is about 128 kg.
comment: One rasher looks tiny. A rasher a day for a year adds up to about 128 kilos.
source: Derived from the 1kg Pork card (Poore & Nemecek 2018 via OWID, 12.3 per kg)
note: Changed from 0.14 on 27 Sep 2026: 0.14 implied 5 kg per kg, half the pork card. 12.3 x 0.028 kg = 0.34. Range 0.2-0.45 by rasher size.

title: 1 New Electric Car
comparison: ~3x lower lifetime emissions than a new petrol car
comment: EVs break even against petrol cars after about 2 to 3 years of use, and their lifetime emissions stay significantly lower.

title: Paris Olympics Visit
comparison: 1.6 Mt total across 13 to 16 million visitors
comment: That's lower than Tokyo's footprint, and about half the impact of the London Olympics.
action_title: Choose a local or low-travel event for your next big trip
action_desc: A single major sporting event visit can cost 125 kg CO₂. Choosing an event within driving distance makes a big difference.
action_saving: ~125 kg CO₂ saved per trip avoided

title: 1 Laptop
comparison: Same as flying Dublin to London and back
comment: About 75% of a laptop's total footprint happens during manufacturing, before you even switch it on.
action_title: Repair or refurbish your laptop instead of buying new
action_desc: A new laptop produces ~300 kg CO₂ in manufacturing alone. Most repairs cost a fraction of that, and extend its life by years.

title: Dublin–Madrid Flight
comparison: 2.2 tonnes/year for 4 yearly trips
comment: Aviation makes up 2.5% of global emissions, and it's very unevenly distributed, a small share of people fly the most.
action_title: Replace one short-haul flight with a train or ferry
action_desc: A return Dublin–Madrid flight produces ~550 kg CO₂. For journeys under 5–6 hours, train is usually feasible and far lower impact.

title: 1 Year Digital Life
comparison: 1844 kg/year for a 2.9-person household
comment: The digital sector's share of global GHG stands at 4% today and is projected to climb to 14% by 2040.
action_title: Enable downloads instead of streaming this week
action_desc: Streaming constantly uses data centres. Downloading music or videos on Wi-Fi, then watching offline, cuts that energy use significantly.
action_saving: Part of your ~636 kg/year digital footprint

title: 1 Year Pet Dog
comparison: Similar to a return flight from Dublin to New York
comment: Most of a dog's footprint comes from their meat-based food, switching to a lower-carbon brand makes a real difference.
action_title: Switch your dog to a lower-impact food brand
action_desc: A dog's annual footprint is ~770 kg CO₂, mostly from meat-based food. Several brands now offer lower-carbon recipes with insect or plant protein.

title: 1 Ton Cement
comparison: ~200 kg for a 10 m² terrace (10 cm thick)
comment: Cement production accounts for about 8% of global CO₂ emissions, more than all the world's trucks combined. That's not some small industry hiding in the background.
action_title: Ask about lower-carbon materials for your next home project
action_desc: Cement production is highly carbon-intensive. For patios, paths or small builds, alternatives like recycled aggregate or timber can be used.

title: 1 Year Food Waste
comparison: ~30% of food is wasted
comment: Wasted food generates methane as it breaks down, so cutting it back is one of the biggest opportunities out there.
action_title: Plan your meals this week to reduce food waste
action_desc: The average household wastes enough food to produce 1,600 kg CO₂ a year. A simple weekly plan and checking your fridge before shopping can cut that by half.

title: NY–London Flight
comparison: Business class is even higher
comment: Aviation accounts for 2.5% of global emissions, and it's spread very unevenly, a small share of frequent flyers rack up most of it.
action_title: Offset your next long-haul flight, and consider flying less
action_desc: A return NY–London flight produces ~1,800 kg CO₂. High-quality carbon offsets through Gold Standard can neutralise that while you reduce flying long-term.

title: $10K in a Dirty Bank
comparison: More than flying return from Dublin to Australia
comment: Between 20 and 30% of bank lending goes to carbon-intensive industry. Where your money sits matters more than I realised.
action_title: Check if your bank funds fossil fuels, and consider switching
action_desc: €10K in a fossil-fuel-lending bank generates ~2,400 kg CO₂/year through loans. Green banks like Triodos exist and are fully regulated.

title: New Small Car
comparison: Same as an average Irish person's entire carbon footprint for 5 months
comment: Even the smallest new car carries a large manufacturing footprint, second-hand is always the lower-carbon choice.
action_title: Consider a second-hand or electric car for your next purchase
action_desc: Manufacturing a new small car produces ~4,000 kg CO₂. Buying second-hand avoids that entirely. EVs have a lower lifetime footprint even accounting for the battery.
action_saving: ~4000 kg CO₂ saved vs. new petrol car

title: New Range Rover
comparison: Same as heating an Irish home for nearly 6 years
comment: One of the highest manufacturing footprints of any consumer product you can buy. I did not see that coming from a car.
action_title: Consider a smaller second-hand or electric vehicle next time
action_desc: A new Range Rover produces ~25,000 kg CO₂ in manufacturing, one of the highest of any consumer product. Even a new mid-size EV is dramatically lower.
action_saving: ~20000+ kg CO₂ saved vs. new large SUV

title: 1kg Asparagus
comparison: Flown from Peru it jumps to ~12 kg CO₂, 30x higher
comment: Asparagus is often imported out of season. Shipped from Peru it rises to 0.67 kg, but flown it can reach almost 12 kg.

title: 1 Litre of Tap Water
comparison: Two litres a day for a whole year is only about 0.1 kg.
comment: I nearly missed this one. Tap water barely registers at all.
source: ADEME Impact CO2 (Agribalyse 3.2), Eau du robinet
note: 0.000132 kg per litre, French tap water.

title: 1 Cup of Tea
sub: With a splash of milk, kettle boiled
comparison: A cup a day for a year is about 15 kg.
comment: The splash of milk has a bigger footprint than the tea itself. I did not expect that.
source: ADEME Impact CO2 (Agribalyse 3.2), Thé and Lait de vache
note: Derived: 225 ml tea x 0.0436/L = 0.010, plus 25 ml milk x 1.15/L = 0.029, total 0.039.

title: 1 Apple
comparison: An apple a day for a year is about 24 kg.
comment: Apples are one of the lightest foods in the data. A good snack for the planet too.
source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018 (Apples 0.43 kg per kg)
note: Derived: 0.43 x 0.15 kg = 0.0645. Global average, land use to retail.

title: 1 Can of Fizzy Drink
comparison: A can a day for a year is about 60 kg.
comment: About 70% of it is packaging and transport, not the drink inside.
source: ADEME Impact CO2 (Agribalyse 3.2), Soda

title: 1 Glass of Wine
comparison: A full 750 ml bottle is about 0.95 kg.
comment: More than half the footprint of wine is the glass bottle. The grapes are the small part.
source: ADEME Impact CO2 (Agribalyse 3.2), Vin
note: Derived: 1.269/L x 0.175 = 0.222. Packaging 54%. OWID wine 1.79/kg would give 0.31.

title: 1 Flat White
sub: Café coffee with milk, conventional beans
comparison: One a day for a year is about 124 kg.
comment: A latte has more milk, so it comes in higher, about 0.55 kg. The milk adds up.
source: The Conversation (Keele University analysis, 2021)
note: Exact figure in the source. Conventional coffee at 15.33 kg per kg green coffee.

title: 1kg Lentils
sub: Dried lentils, green, blond or red
comparison: The 1kg of beef card is about 60 times more.
comment: Lentils give you protein for a tiny footprint. Kilo for kilo, beef is a whole different planet.
source: ADEME Impact CO2 (Agribalyse 3.2), Lentilles
note: 0.58 per kg, farm to shop. OWID other pulses 1.79.

title: 1 Egg and Cress Sandwich
comparison: The all-day breakfast sandwich in the same study was 1.44 kg, nearly double.
comment: Making your own sandwich can cut its footprint by about half. Easy one.
source: University of Manchester, Espinoza-Orias & Azapagic 2018
note: 739 g, lowest ready-made sandwich in the study (UK). Includes packaging, retail refrigeration and waste.

title: 1 Sliced Pan
sub: 800 g loaf of sliced white bread
comparison: That's about 0.06 kg per slice across 20 slices.
comment: Bread is a small footprint per slice. Wasting half the loaf still doubles it though.
source: ADEME Impact CO2 (Agribalyse 3.2), Pain de mie
note: Derived: 1.559 per kg x 0.8 = 1.25. French sandwich bread as a proxy for an Irish sliced pan.

title: 1kg Beet Sugar
comparison: Cane sugar in the same data is 3.2 kg per kg, almost double.
comment: Where sugar comes from matters. Beet sugar came out lower than cane sugar in the data I found.
source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018

title: 1kg Tomatoes
comparison: About 4.5 times 1kg of potatoes in the same study (0.46 kg).
comment: I thought tomatoes would be light. They're heavier than potatoes, apples and onions.
source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018

title: 1kg Porridge Oats
comparison: A 40 g bowl made with water is about 0.1 kg.
comment: Oats are a light breakfast. Make porridge with a glass of milk and the milk outweighs the oats.
source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018 (Oatmeal)

title: 1 Meal with Beef
comparison: Nearly 6 times a vegetarian meal (0.85 kg).
comment: Same plate, swap the beef, and the footprint drops by more than 80%. That's a big lever.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Repas avec du boeuf

title: 1 Bowl of Lamb Stew
sub: Welsh cawl with bread and butter
comparison: About 4 portions of fish and chips (1.5 kg each).
comment: Three quarters of this stew's footprint comes from the lamb. Sheep burp methane as they digest.
source: WWF UK, Food in a Warming World (2018)

title: 1kg Pork
comparison: About 1.2 times the 1kg of chicken card (9.9 kg).
comment: Pork sits between chicken and beef. Still a lot more than any plant I've checked.
source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018 (Pig Meat)
note: 12.31 per kg, global. ADEME pork 6.67. Checked 27 Sep 2026 against Irish data: Teagasc/Bord Bia calculator 5.52 per kg pigmeat at the farm gate builds to about 13-16 on the full boundary, no lower than OWID, so the global figure stays.

title: 1kg Prawns
comparison: A 200 g pack is about 4 kg.
comment: Prawns surprised me. Per kilo they're heavier than chicken or pork.
source: ADEME Impact CO2 (Agribalyse 3.2), Crevettes

title: 1kg Dark Chocolate
comparison: A 100 g bar is about 4.7 kg.
comment: Chocolate was a shock. Kilo for kilo, dark chocolate beats lamb in the global data.
source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018
note: 46.65 per kg vs lamb 39.72 in the same dataset. Includes land-use change.

title: 1 Week of Food
comparison: About 1,900 kg over a year.
comment: To stay on track, a day of food needs to drop from 5.17 kg to about 4.09 kg by 2030.
source: WWF UK, Food in a Warming World (2018)
note: Derived: 5.17 per person per day x 7 = 36.2. UK.

title: 1 Year of Bottled Water
sub: One litre a day, plastic bottles
comparison: The same amount of tap water is about 0.05 kg.
comment: Almost all of it is the bottle and the lorry. The water itself is nothing.
source: ADEME Impact CO2 (Agribalyse 3.2), Eau en bouteille

title: 365 Lattes
sub: One café latte a day for a year
comparison: Same year of lattes with sustainably grown coffee: about 120 kg.
comment: Coffee grown sustainably would cut each latte to about 0.33 kg. Farming choices matter.
source: The Conversation (Keele University analysis, 2021)

title: 1kg Rice
comparison: A 75 g portion is about 0.33 kg.
comment: Rice is heavier than wheat or oats. Flooded paddy fields give off methane.
source: Our World in Data, Poore & Nemecek 2018
note: 4.45 per kg. ADEME rice 2.01. 12% below Meal with Beef 4.97.

title: 5km Taxi Ride
comparison: A short taxi hop makes a bit more CO2 than one dishwasher cycle.
comment: Taxis are handy, but for 5km a bike or the Luas does the job with far less CO2.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (regular taxi)
note: 0.18558 kg CO2e per passenger-km (incl. WTT) x 5 km.

title: Dublin–Holyhead Ferry, Foot Passenger
comparison: Taking a car on board makes the same crossing roughly seven times higher.
comment: Walking onto the ferry is one of the gentlest ways to leave the island. The car is what makes it heavy.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (ferry, foot passenger)

title: Dublin to Galway by Coach
comparison: Driving it alone in an average petrol car would be about six times more.
comment: Same road, same city at the end. Sharing a coach with loads of people shrinks my share of the CO2.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (coach)

title: Dublin to Belfast by Electric Car
sub: About 170km on the Irish grid, driver only
comparison: The same trip in an average petrol car is about 35 kg, four times more.
comment: Irish wind power helps here. As the grid gets greener, this number keeps shrinking.
source: SEAI Energy in Ireland 2024 (253.7 g CO2/kWh) and UK DESNZ 2025 EV energy use (0.20656 kWh/km)
note: 170 km x 0.20656 kWh/km x 0.2537. Charging only.

title: 100km by Bus
comparison: A long-distance coach does the same 100km for about 3.4 kg per person.
comment: Town buses stop and start all day and aren't always full. Fill them up and each seat gets cleaner.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (local bus)

title: Dublin to Galway by Motorbike
comparison: About four times the same trip by coach.
comment: Two wheels sounds light, but a petrol motorbike still burns plenty. The coach beats it easily.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (motorbike, average)

title: Dublin–London Return Flight
sub: Economy, Dublin to Heathrow and back
comparison: Like driving an average petrol car about 640km.
comment: It's a short hop, but take-off burns loads of fuel. Rail and sail gets you there too.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (short-haul economy, with radiative forcing)

title: Dublin–Paris Return Flight
sub: Economy, Dublin to Charles de Gaulle and back
comparison: That's over 900 kWh of Irish electricity.
comment: A weekend in Paris by plane costs the sky more than people think.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (short-haul economy, with radiative forcing)

title: Dublin–Tenerife Return Flight
sub: Economy, Dublin to Tenerife South and back
comparison: More than a whole year of owning a pet dog (770 kg).
comment: Sunshine is tempting after an Irish winter. But this trip alone is a big slice of a yearly carbon budget.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (short-haul economy, with radiative forcing)

title: Dublin–Los Angeles Return Flight
comparison: Over two years of a typical Irish home's electricity.
comment: From up in space, planes look tiny. This one trip outweighs two years of lights, fridge and telly at home.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (long-haul economy, with radiative forcing)

title: Dublin–Sydney Return Flight
comparison: More than building a new small car (4,000 kg).
comment: Halfway round the world and back. That's more CO2 than making a whole new car.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (long-haul economy, with radiative forcing)

title: Boiling a Full Kettle
comparison: You could boil about 14 full kettles for the CO2 of one dishwasher cycle.
comment: One kettle is tiny. Only boil what you need and it gets even tinier.
source: SEAI Energy in Ireland 2024 (253.7 g CO2/kWh)
note: Physics: 1.7 L x 90 K heating = 0.178 kWh, about 0.2 kWh with losses x 0.2537.

title: 1kWh of Irish Electricity
comparison: Four kWh of Irish electricity makes about 1 kg of CO2.
comment: This is the magic number for Ireland. Every unit you use is about a quarter of a kilo.
source: SEAI Energy in Ireland 2024, Appendix (electricity 2023: 253.7 g CO2/kWh)
world_source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2024 (world average 480 g CO2 per kWh in 2023)

title: 10 Min Electric Shower
comparison: About the same as boiling 8 full kettles.
comment: The electric shower is one of the hungriest things per hour in an Irish home. Shorter showers help.
source: SEAI Energy in Ireland 2024 (253.7 g CO2/kWh); 9.5kW typical rating

title: 1 Hour of a Plug-in Heater
comparison: The same as boiling about 10 full kettles.
comment: Plug-in heaters feel cosy but they turn every unit straight into heat. A heat pump does far more with the same electricity.
source: SEAI Energy in Ireland 2024 (253.7 g CO2/kWh)

title: 1 Hour of Patio Heater
comparison: One hour outdoors equals about 12 kWh of Irish electricity.
comment: Heating the open sky. I'd rather grab a jumper and a blanket.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (propane, 0.23258 kg CO2e/kWh)

title: 2 Bales of Peat Briquettes
comparison: Nearly double driving 100km in a petrol car (25 kg).
comment: Irish bogs held this carbon for thousands of years. Burning a couple of bales lets it all out in an evening or two.
source: SEAI Energy in Ireland 2024, Appendix (peat briquettes 98.9 t CO2/TJ, 18.55 MJ/kg)
note: 1.835 kg CO2 per kg x 25 kg.

title: 1 New Washing Machine
comparison: The same as about 490 washes at 40°C.
comment: Most of a washing machine's carbon is spent before it arrives. Fixing the old one often wins.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Électroménager (lave-linge)

title: 1 Year of Home Electricity
comparison: Works out at nearly 3 kg of CO2 every day.
comment: All the lights, the fridge, the telly and the washing, added up. More wind on the grid shrinks this every year.
source: CRU typical consumption 4,200 kWh (Electric Ireland) x SEAI 2023 253.7 g/kWh

title: 500 Litres of Heating Oil
comparison: Each litre burned releases about 2.5 kg of CO2.
comment: Loads of Irish homes still heat with oil. A well-insulated house needs far fewer top-ups.
source: UK DESNZ GHG Conversion Factors 2025 (burning oil, 2.54016 kg CO2e/litre)

title: 1 Web Search
sub: Device, network and data centre share
comparison: It takes around 800 searches to make 1 kg of CO2e.
comment: One search is tiny. But billions of people search every day, so the tiny bits pile up fast.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Usage numérique (Base Empreinte)

title: 1 Hour of Video Call
comparison: About the same as driving 400 metres in a petrol or diesel car.
comment: I video call my crew back home a lot. Turning the camera off when it's not needed makes each call lighter.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Usage numérique (visioconférence)

title: 100 AI Chatbot Replies
sub: Medium-length replies from one large model
comparison: One reply is about 1.14 g, roughly the same as one web search.
comment: Asking a chatbot feels free. Each answer still runs on real machines in real buildings using real electricity.
source: Mistral AI life cycle analysis with Carbone 4 and ADEME, July 2025
note: 1.14 g per 400-token Mistral Large 2 reply. One company's model.

title: 1 TB in the Cloud for a Year
comparison: About the same as driving 1.7 km in a petrol or diesel car.
comment: The cloud isn't in the sky. It's big buildings full of humming drives. Deleting old files helps a little.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, stockage de données dans le cloud
note: 0.000235 kg per GB per year x 1,000. French grid.

title: 1 Year of a Refurbished Phone
sub: Per year of use, vs about 26 kg for a new phone
comparison: A new phone works out at about 26 kg a year, so refurbished saves around 23 kg.
comment: A second-hand phone skips most of the factory part. Same calls, same photos, far less carbon.
source: ADEME/Arcep 2022, produits reconditionnés
note: 23 kg avoided per year = 87% reduction, so about 3.4 kg per year.

title: 1 Smartwatch
comparison: You could make nearly nine of these for one new smartphone's 70 kg.
comment: Small gadget, small footprint. But I count every one, and people often own lots of them.
source: Apple, Apple Watch Series 11 Product Environmental Report, Sept 2025

title: 1 Pair of Wireless Earbuds
comparison: About the same as driving 90 km in a petrol or diesel car.
comment: Earbuds are tiny, but the batteries and chips inside take real energy to make. Look after them.
source: Apple, AirPods Pro 3 Product Environmental Report, Sept 2025
note: Full lifecycle incl. case and packaging. One manufacturer.

title: 1 Tablet
comparison: About 1.2 times the carbon of making one new smartphone (70 kg).
comment: Most of a tablet's carbon is spent before you switch it on. Keeping it longer is the big win.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Numérique (tablette)

title: 1 Games Console
comparison: Five years of play adds another 538 kg in Microsoft's US estimate.
comment: Making the console is only the start. Most of its carbon comes later, from the electricity used to play it.
source: Microsoft, Xbox Series X Ecoprofile, Oct 2023
note: Production 190 kg incl. controller, cables and packaging.

title: 1 TV
comparison: Making it is 328 kg of that, about 89%.
comment: A telly's biggest carbon cost happens in the factory. Keeping one for years beats upgrading.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Numérique (télévision)
note: 328 manufacturing + 29.6 use (French grid, 8 years) + 11.9 end of life.

title: 1 Recycled Cotton Jumper
comparison: About a sixth of a new wool jumper (52.9 kg).
comment: Recycled cotton skips growing new cotton. That's where a lot of the carbon hides.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Habillement (pull en coton recyclé)

title: 1 Cotton Shirt
comparison: Almost twice a fast fashion t-shirt (6 kg).
comment: More fabric, more stitching, more carbon. A good shirt worn for years spreads that out nicely.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Habillement (chemise en coton)

title: 1 Faux Leather Jacket
comparison: About the same as driving 170 km in a petrol or diesel car.
comment: Faux leather is mostly plastic made from oil. It's not animal, but it's not carbon-free either.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Habillement (veste simili-cuir)

title: 1 Rain Jacket
comparison: About 20% more than a pair of jeans (33 kg).
comment: In Ireland a rain jacket is basically survival gear. Buy one good one and wear it for years.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Habillement (veste imperméable)

title: 1 Wool Jumper
comparison: About six and a half recycled cotton jumpers (8.1 kg each).
comment: Wool is warm and natural, but sheep burp methane. Most of this jumper's carbon comes from the farm.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Habillement (pull en laine)

title: 1 Winter Coat
comparison: About the same as 14 fast fashion t-shirts (6 kg each).
comment: A big coat is a big carbon bill. Wear it for many winters and each one costs much less.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Habillement (manteau)

title: 1 Home Football Match
comparison: About the same as driving 12 km in a petrol or diesel car.
comment: Walking, cycling or taking the bus to the match makes a real difference. So does sharing the car.
source: Dosumu, Colbeck & Bragg (2017), Scientific Reports 7:6986

title: 1 Away Football Match
comparison: About eight times a home fan's trip (1.7 kg).
comment: Following your team away means long drives. Supporters' buses fill every seat, and that helps.
source: Dosumu, Colbeck & Bragg (2017), Scientific Reports 7:6986
note: 13.71 kg per away spectator, travel only.

title: 1 Pair of Sports Shoes
comparison: About the same as driving 130 km in a petrol or diesel car.
comment: Good trainers carry you a long way. Resoling or passing them on stretches their carbon further.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Habillement (chaussures de sport)

title: 1 Day Skiing
sub: Per skier, travel, lifts, lodging, food, kit
comparison: More than half of it, 52%, is just getting there.
comment: Snow is magic. But getting to the mountains is most of the carbon, so train travel helps loads.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Cas pratiques (journée au ski)

title: 1 Year of Marathon Running
sub: Training plus a race in New York, one runner
comparison: The transatlantic flight alone is 3,560 kg, about 83% of it.
comment: Running itself is almost carbon-free. Flying to a race is what makes the number jump.
source: Castaignède et al. (2021), Int. J. Environ. Res. Public Health 18(5):2769
note: Same year with a local race was 730 kg.

title: 1 Rugby Team's World Cup Flights
comparison: About 3,100 kg for each of the 45 people on board.
comment: Top teams fly a lot. One return trip for one squad is a mountain of carbon.
source: ADEME Impact CO2, Cas pratiques (A/R Johannesburg-Paris d'une équipe de rugby)
note: 45 people x 17,462 km x ADEME long-haul factor. Scenario, not a measured charter.

title: 1 m³ of Sawn Timber
comparison: The wood also holds about 741 kg of CO2 taken from the air while the tree grew.
comment: Wood is the lightest builder here. The tree pulled carbon from the air and keeps it locked in the beams.
source: SCA Wood AB, EPD NEPD-3442-2053, 2022
note: GWP-fossil A1-A3; biogenic carbon not counted.

title: 1 m³ of Low-Carbon Concrete
comparison: About 27% less than the same concrete with no GGBS (218 kg).
comment: Swap some cement for GGBS, a leftover from steelmaking, and the same concrete gets much lighter on carbon.
source: Irish Concrete Federation EPD, C28/35 Readymix (30% GGBS), June 2025

title: 1 m³ of Concrete
comparison: One cubic metre weighs about 2.4 tonnes.
comment: Concrete is everywhere in Irish homes. Most of its carbon comes from the cement that glues it together.
source: Irish Concrete Federation EPD, C28/35 Readymix (0% GGBS), June 2025

title: 1,000 Bricks
comparison: That's about 0.45 kg for every single brick.
comment: Bricks are baked in hot kilns, and that heat usually comes from gas. A thousand bricks adds up.
source: Brick Development Association, BRE EPD 000002, 2019
note: 213 kg per tonne x 2.13 kg per brick.

title: 1 Tonne of Recycled Steel
sub: Scrap melted in an electric furnace
comparison: About a third of average steel's 2,180 kg.
comment: Melting old steel with electricity beats making new steel from ore and coal. Scrap is precious.
source: worldsteel, Sustainability Indicators 2025

title: 1 Tonne of Steel
comparison: About three times recycled steel (710 kg).
comment: Steel holds up bridges and buildings. Most of it is still made with coal, which is why it's so heavy on carbon.
source: worldsteel, Sustainability Indicators 2025

title: 1 New Semi-Detached Home
sub: Irish 118 m² semi, materials and building
comparison: About 411 kg for every square metre of the house.
comment: Before anyone moves in, a new Irish semi has already caused about 48 tonnes. Reusing buildings saves a lot.
source: Construct Innovate / Irish Green Building Council, INDICATE, 2025
note: 411 kg per m² x 118 m² upfront (A1-A5). Only 4 case studies.
